# FDG5092

> DO NOT throw exceptions from implicit conversion operators.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.7.2 Conversion Operators.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1065
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

CA1065 reports an exception thrown directly in an implicit conversion operator; in a probe with SDK 10.0.402 it reported an ArgumentException thrown there. Exceptions from methods that the operator calls are not seen. CA1065 also reports other members, such as Equals, GetHashCode, property getters and finalizers, which FDG5031 and FDG5054 cover in part and this rule does not. The fix changes behavior, not a signature; CA1065 has no code fix.

## From the book

It is very difficult for end users to understand what is happening, because they might not be aware that a conversion is taking place.

> **Stephen Toub:** From a performance perspective, implicit conversions should also avoid allocations or otherwise having nontrivial overhead. Just as with boxing, if an implicit conversion is expensive, it’s likely developers will end up paying these costs without realizing it.
